seo.meta_title: What Does 화 Mean? | Fire, Anger and Flower in One Korean Syllable
seo.meta_description: 화 can mean fire, anger or flower. AI picks one meaning. Learn how (G)I-DLE's 화(火花) plays on it, and how to use 화나다 and 화 풀어 in real life.

ai_failure.situation: You see (G)I-DLE's 2021 song title 화(火花) and ask an AI tool to translate it.
ai_failure.ai_mistake: Gives a single meaning, such as 'Fire' or 'Anger', without explaining the characters in brackets.
ai_failure.why_it_fails: 화 is one syllable with several meanings from different Chinese characters: 火 (fire) and 花 (flower). Anger is also 화, written with 火 — in Korean, being angry is having fire inside. The title layers these on purpose, and 火花 together means 'spark'.

natural_solution.rule: In everyday Korean, 화 alone almost always means anger. Learn it in set phrases rather than on its own.

alternatives.context: 'Please don't be mad anymore' — literally 'untie your anger', common between partners and friends
Tuesday — the 'fire day' of the week

nuance: Korean week days follow the elements: 월 (moon), 화 (fire), 수 (water), 목 (wood), 금 (metal), 토 (earth), 일 (sun). The fire in 화요일 is the same 火 as in anger. When a single Korean syllable appears in a title with Chinese characters next to it, the characters tell you which meanings the artist wants you to hear.
